title: Denmark plans ban on sharing AI deepfakes without consent
key_facts: Culture Minister Zenia Stampe will propose a bill on Thursday 8 Oct 2026.
It would ban the digital copying and sharing of lifelike representations of a person, including appearance and voice.
Aim: stop the spread of AI-generated deepfakes; get tech giants to take down manipulated content quickly.
Meant to protect the public and artists.
Exception for caricatures, parodies, satire and other work that criticises society and those in power.
Still subject to parliamentary approval; Stampe hopes it enters into force around the turn of the year.
Per The News International, Stampe says courts would decide whether content is real satire.
quote_evidence: Denmark’s culture minister will on Thursday propose a bill to ban the digital copying and sharing of lifelike representations of a person, including their appearance and voice, in a bid to crack down on the spread of AI-generated deepfakes.
“One of the main goals of the bill is to get the tech giants to take down manipulated content quickly so that it causes as little harm as possible,” she said.
why_it_matters_hint: A concrete national ban on non-consensual deepfakes of faces and voices.
